realmDoctrine: Every capital city has normal-case Portal access; the mode label is Portal, not Portal.
Every City and Capital City has Skyship access; deep-water cities use floating upper landing platforms.
Caravans remain on land, marsh decks, bridges, dry upper structures, or explicitly authored platforms.
Ferries and steamships remain on surface water, marsh channels, lagoons, straits, rivers, reefs, floating settlements, or docked water edges.
Submarines serve deep water, floating/ocean-surface settlements, coastal access, and authored airlocked underwater train stations.
Rail may enter mountains, caverns, underwater tunnel stations, bridges, and named cross-province links when the manual canon explicitly supports it.
Weather and moon-tide hazards remain attached to every generated segment.

caravan.label: Caravan
caravan.fare: Standard: 5 Copper - 1 Silver; premium varies for hired guards and enchanted wagons.
caravan.doctrine: Ichor-assisted road service for province roads, wilderness roads, merchant freight, and slower public travel.
caravan.coreRisks: Road weather, cliff edges, bandits, beasts, ichor-lantern leakage, toll-law disputes, and settlement gate delays.
caravan.breakLabel: water, axle, guard-watch, and passenger respite

ferry.label: Ferry
ferry.fare: Standard: 5 Copper - 2 Silver; premium: 4 Silver - 1 Gold for private boat charter.
ferry.doctrine: Short-to-medium harbor, river, lake, canal, reef, and island service.
ferry.coreRisks: Fog, snags, reefs, whirlpools, water predators, false dock lights, and harbor injunctions.
ferry.breakLabel: mooring, rope, bilge, and deck-watch respite

steamship.label: Steamship
steamship.fare: Standard: 1 Silver - 5 Gold; premium: 3 Gold - 8 Platinum for stateroom or charter.
steamship.doctrine: Longer-range surface-water service with ichor-assisted boilers, condenser recovery, and harbor grounding.
steamship.coreRisks: Boiler overpressure, deck sweep, pirate waters, volatile harbors, ballast-water contamination, and condenser fouling.
steamship.breakLabel: boiler-watch, condenser wash, meal, and gangway reset

submarine.label: Submarine
submarine.fare: Standard: 5 Silver - 5 Gold; premium: 10 Gold - 15 Platinum for pressure cabin or research charter.
submarine.doctrine: Underwater, coastal, reef, trench, hidden-port, subcombined-hub, and amphibious lock-to-land service.
submarine.coreRisks: Pressure strain, ballast faults, stale air, hostile deepfolk, abyssal resonance, and lock-collar delay.
submarine.breakLabel: pressure-trim, life-support, ballast, and hull-skin respite

train_rail.label: Train / Rail
train_rail.fare: Standard: 1 Silver; premium: 5 Silver - 1 Gold for private cabins.
train_rail.doctrine: Steel-wheel ichor rail over land corridors, tunnels, bridges, river spans, lake spans, and coastal causeways; no open sea crossings.
train_rail.coreRisks: Rockslides, tunnel pockets, track sabotage, signal fraud, rail ward failure, and elevated wind shear.
train_rail.breakLabel: crew change, brake cooling, traction-stack, and platform reset

skyship.label: Skyship
skyship.fare: Standard: 2 Silver - 3 Gold; premium: 5 Gold - 10 Platinum for private suites or VIP skydeck.
skyship.doctrine: High-altitude intercity and cross-region service using lift lattice, sail-field coupling, grounding rails, and skyport transformation lanes.
skyship.coreRisks: Sky pirates, pressure drops, storm giants, lift-lattice flutter, cargo shift, and dock charge bleed.
skyship.breakLabel: grounding, sail-field, mast, hull-cleansing, and cargo-shift respite

portal.label: Portal
portal.fare: Restricted access. Portal Access Pass required; premium: 2 Gold - 5 Platinum for high-priority travel.
portal.doctrine: Capital-city Portal gate service only; not an all-caps label.
portal.coreRisks: Destination-lock drift, pass suspension, mass-transfer spikes, field overheating, and fail-closed strandings.

fareCollection: Fare collection is part of scheduled dwell time for caravan, ferry, steamship, submarine, train/rail, and skyship service.
portalAccess: Portal Access Pass inspection is part of the portal timetable and may hold a batch before destination lock.
hubRules: Multi-mode hubs receive additional transfer handling time so passengers can cross platforms, piers, lockhouses, sky corridors, and portal vestibules safely.
playerSafeBoundary: The files identify public service, hazards, and operating doctrine while keeping sealed incidents, private manifests, and restricted outcomes outside the public ledger.

timeConversionRules.offsetMethod: Nearest whole-hour longitude band: offsetHours = round(longitude / 15), clamped from BMT-12 to BMT+12.
timeConversionRules.latitudeUse: Latitude is recorded on every settlement certificate and confirms the settlement coordinate and hemisphere; the public hour offset is assigned by longitude so route clocks stay consistent.
timeConversionRules.localClockRule: Every passenger-facing arrival, release, and transfer time is posted in the local time of the settlement where that event happens.
timeConversionRules.originDepartureRule: Published departures are origin-terminal local time. Once the vehicle is in motion, every later stop is converted from absolute elapsed travel time into that stop’s local clock.
timeConversionRules.timeZoneCrossingRule: Eastbound clock crossings move the displayed local clock ahead; westbound clock crossings move it behind. Date labels may move forward or backward when the clock crosses midnight.
timeConversionRules.portalRule: Portal crossings obey the same settlement-local clock ledger. A portal can create a large visible clock jump because the traveler changes longitude almost at once, even when the controlled crossing itself is short.
timeConversionRules.wednesdayRule: Wednesday schedules keep their slower movement and added ichor checks, then receive the same local settlement time conversion.

timeZonePolicy.passengerRule: Station boards show local time for that settlement. Route ledgers preserve BMT for dispatchers.
timeZonePolicy.transferRule: Transfers use the receiving settlement local time after release clearance.
timeZonePolicy.portalRule: Portal crossings obey the same settlement-local clock ledger. A portal can create a large visible clock jump because the traveler changes longitude almost at once, even when the controlled crossing itself is short.
timeZonePolicy.missedConnectionRule: If a time-zone crossing moves the local clock backward, the arrival remains tied to the absolute BMT ledger so passengers cannot reuse the same local hour twice for fare claims.

caravan.label: Caravan
caravan.rule: Surface roads follow passable land, valley, forest, marsh, and cavern-mouth approaches; deep cavern stops require lift roads, switchbacks, and waystation air shafts.

rail.label: Train / Rail
rail.rule: Rail routes use storm-brass track, tunnel grades, sealed cavern stations, and bridgeworks; rail does not cross open ocean without a named causeway, tunnel, or ferry/submarine transfer.

ferry.label: Ferry
ferry.rule: Ferry routes are local/short water crossings, marsh canals, bay hops, and harbor-mouth shuttles; they avoid exposed open sea and abyssal pressure routes.

steamship.label: Steamship
steamship.rule: Steamship routes serve ocean-surface, coastal, bay, gulf, sea, strait, and floating-settlement docks; underwater stops require surface lift docks or submarine transfer.

submarine.label: Submarine
submarine.rule: Submarine routes serve underwater, ocean-surface, reef, trench, deep-sea, and mixed coastal locks with pressure-gate certification.

skyship.label: Skyship
skyship.rule: Skyship routes connect city/capital-grade towers, mountain shelves, floating towers, and storm-cleared landing rings; severe crosswinds alter schedules.

portal.label: Portal
portal.rule: Portal routes connect capital-grade civic gates only; weather affects staging/crowd control, not physical crossing time.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Train / Rail
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Land-only train route. Do not use for ocean, lake, river-only, subcombined, or sky routes.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Caravan
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Ground route for road, wilderness, market, or freight transit service.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Ferry
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Short-to-medium surface water route for lakes, rivers, harbors, canals, reefs, and nearby islands.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Skyship
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Air route for high terrain, island chains, skyports, and long-distance crossings.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Portal
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Permit-only restricted route with Portal Access Pass inspection and Wednesday recalibration.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Steamship
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Longer-range surface-water passenger service for coastal or major sea-lane travel.

routeTypeHeaders.title: Submarine
routeTypeHeaders.disclaimer: Underwater route for reefs, trenches, deep-sea settlements, and subcombined hubs.

fares: Land-only rail. It can serve cities, towns, tunnels, bridges, and mountain corridors, but it does not travel across open water or underwater routes.
Best for local roads, roads through wilderness, merchant freight, and slower transit movement.
Short-to-medium water service for harbors, rivers, lakes, canals, reefs, and islands.
Premium long-distance air service for mountains, islands, and terrain that land routes cannot easily cross.
Permit-based travel. Use for official, scholarly, military, emergency, or restricted transit corridors.
Longer-range surface-water transit and passenger service; slower than portals or skyships but excellent for coastal chains and major sea lanes.
10 Gold - 15 Platinum (Private Pressure Cabin / Research Charter)
Underwater transit service for deep-sea settlements, reefs, trenches, hidden ports, and subcombined transit hubs.

routeRewriteDoctrine.deepCavernRule: Deep cavern settlements are not surface-only stops; routes must include lift/tunnel/airshaft/under-road access language and weather risk.
routeRewriteDoctrine.deepSeaRule: Underwater/deep sea settlements require submarine pressure gates, ocean locks, or surface transfer docks; steamship/ferry cannot pretend to directly enter pressure settlements.
routeRewriteDoctrine.namedFeatureRule: Route names and segment references use canonical named highlands, rivers, deltas, seas, bays, gulfs, forests, vents, and weather landmarks from the helper folder.
routeRewriteDoctrine.weatherRule: Clear public service timetable remains baseline; active weather adjusts movement time and risk per segment.
routeRewriteDoctrine.modeSurfaceRule: Raw helper transit tags are checked against updated realism hex terrain. Trains and caravans are removed from pure water/deep-pressure/floating-only stops; ferries and steamships are removed from pure land and deep-pressure-only stops; submarines are allowed only for deep water, floating/ocean-surface, and coastal access.
routeRewriteDoctrine.ferryDistanceRule: Ferry routes are generated only as short surface-water crossings at or below 750 km per segment; longer surface-water service is steamship and deeper service is submarine.

canonicalRevision.spatialAuthority: Final 2048 x 1024 equirectangular anchors and province transforms from the corrected geological/weather compendium override every earlier coordinate, UTC, mapped-biome/depth, and route geometry value.
canonicalRevision.nonSpatialAuthority: Current pantheon/races and life compendia preserve and extend non-spatial canon; the newest night-sky/time compendium governs calendar, celestial, and exact settlement UTC data.
